questions.q: Write one comparative sentence about how each writer feels during the journey.
questions.a: Text One's writer is frightened, gripping the rail, whereas Text Two's writer is calm and even amused by complaining travellers.
questions.model: Frame: 'Text One's writer feels..., shown by..., whereas Text Two's writer feels..., shown by...'.

questions.q: Find one similarity in what the journey teaches.
questions.a: Both show that travel changes people: gratitude in Text One, better character in Text Two.

questions.q: Core: complete the comparison grid (four rows), then write an introduction and one integrated paragraph in the portal response box. Starter: 'Both writers...'
questions.a: A completed grid and an integrated paragraph comparing ideas and methods with evidence from both texts.
questions.model: Teacher completes row 1 of the grid and the introduction with the class before pupils continue alone.

questions.q: Extend: add a second integrated paragraph on voice (first person and imperatives).
questions.a: Text One's 'I' draws us into one experience, whereas Text Two's imperatives instruct all travellers.

questions.q: Stretch: explain how the difference in period helps explain their perspectives.
questions.a: A nineteenth-century guide expects stoicism; a modern memoir values honesty about fear.

questions.q: An answer on only one text in Q7...
questions.a: A) cannot reach the top levels

questions.q: Answer the ponder with one reason from each text.
questions.a: For example: Text Two's writer, because his patience and calm ('fix his eye upon the horizon') would steady me.
